description: DWSIM Shortcut Column (DSTWU) on benzene/toluene, preceded by a heater that sets the feed condition.
notes: Algorithm recovered from the numbers (all reproduced by thermo-sim, see tests/test_dstwu.py): DWSIM evaluates alpha = K_LK / K_HK once, at the state of the feed stream (370 K, 1.01325 bar, two phases), and uses it in both Fenske (ln[(xD_LK/xD_HK)(xB_HK/xB_LK)] / ln alpha = 6.76392) and Underwood (theta = 1.61215, Rmin = 1.84130). The mean of the values at the top and bottom would give 6.7007 (arithmetic) and 1.8225.
Gilliland: the Eduljee form Y = 0.75 (1 - X^0.5668) with X = (R - Rmin)/(R + 1) and Y = (N - Nmin)/(N + 1) gives N = 11.49027 (DWSIM 11.4903). The Molokanov form gives 11.699.

Optimum feed stage 5.74513 is N/2. The cases 70/30 and 90/10 (additional_cases) show the rule: DWSIM reports N * n_S / (n_R + n_S) with n_R = ln[(xD_LK/xD_HK)(z_HK/z_LK)] and n_S = ln[(z_LK/z_HK)(xB_HK/xB_LK)] (Fenske minimum stages of each section with one alpha), that is the number of stages BELOW the feed (counted from the bottom): 70/30 gives 6.2662 of 9.732 (0.6438), 90/10 gives 7.3362 of 8.403 (0.873). Kirkbride (exponent 0.206) gives 0.41 / 0.26 of the stages above the feed and does not fit. With 50/50 the ratio is 1, so that case alone could not tell.
Internal flows: L = R D = 150, V = (R + 1) D = 200, L' = L + q F with q = 0.278375 (liquid fraction of the feed) = 177.8375, V' = V - (1 - q) F = 127.8375 mol/s.
Condenser duty = V (H_dew - H_bubble) of the distillate composition: 6125.98 kW with thermo-sim (DWSIM 6125.74). Reboiler duty follows from the overall energy balance (3836.09 against 3836.37).

The DWSIM input 'heavy key mole fraction' 0.05 is the HK in the DISTILLATE (distillate 0.95/0.05, bottoms 0.05/0.95). The description of the task says 'HK in bottoms'; the stream table settles it. The report prints the light key empty.

Estimated column height = 0.5 * (N + 2) in the three cases (6.74513, 5.20128, 5.86603 m, N = 11.4903, 8.40256, 9.73205); with tray height 0.5 m tray_height * N + 1 m is the same formula, so another stage height is needed to tell them apart. Diameter not implemented: D / sqrt(V_rect[mol/s]) = 0.22018, 0.22020, 0.22019 in the three cases (V_rect = 200, 377.776, 288.888 mol/s), so D scales with sqrt(V); the proportionality constant (0.7439 m/s of superficial vapor velocity at the distillate density 2.782 kg/m3) is unknown.

Product streams leave at the bubble point (distillate 353.857 K, bottoms 381.532 K, the tiny vapor fractions are the numerical tolerance of DWSIM). thermo-sim bubble temperatures: 353.857 and 381.532 K.

Liquid enthalpies of thermo-sim are 0.1 to 0.3 % more negative than DWSIM (distillate -25604 against -25563, bottoms -23670 against -23597 kJ/kmol, sensible values), which is the 0.5 % difference in the bottoms energy flow and 0.15 % in the heater duty.

Feed K for a single-phase feed: DWSIM evaluates K = phi_L / phi_V with the incipient phase of a stability trial. For the 70/30 vapor feed at 370 K the 'liquid' composition in its stream table (0.494523 / 0.505477) is the fixed point x = z / K normalized (thermo-sim 0.494526 / 0.505474) and the fugacity coefficients of that liquid reproduce its table; alpha = 2.38499 (DWSIM Nmin implies 2.3853).

Subcooled liquid feed (additional_cases.feed_90_10_subcooled): the trial-vapor symmetry of the vapor-feed rule is confirmed (alpha 3.2851 from the stream fugacity coefficients, 3.2851 in thermo-sim), and Nmin, Rmin, N and feed stage agree to 0.03 %. The height 0.5 (N + 2) = 3.74275 m is a fourth data point.

additional_cases.description: Same heater (300 K to 370 K), column (R = 3, x_LK,B = x_HK,D = 0.05, 1.01325 bar, total condenser, stage height 0.5 m) and feed flow 100 mol/s, with another feed composition. At 370 K both feeds are 100 % vapor.

feed_90_10.note: DWSIM rounds the bottoms flow to 5.56 mol/s (exact 5.5556), which moves its bottoms toluene fraction to 0.949281 instead of 0.95.

feed_90_10_subcooled.description: Same column and 90/10 feed, but the feed enters the column directly at 300 K as subcooled liquid (no heater, vapor fraction 8.9e-16, q = 1).
feed_90_10_subcooled.note: Rmin is negative (Underwood with q = 1 and a large alpha); DWSIM still runs with R = 3 and thermo-sim reproduces it. For a liquid feed K = phi_L(z) / phi_V(y*) with y* the trial vapor, which is the 'vapor' composition of the DWSIM stream table (0.967284 / 0.032717).

partial_condenser_50_50.description: Same 50/50 feed, heater and specification as the base case but with a partial condenser (vapor distillate).
partial_condenser_50_50.note: The separation, Rmin, Nmin, N, feed stage, internal flows and reboiler duty are identical to the total condenser case. The distillate is saturated vapor at its dew point (355.311 K) and Qc = L * (H_dew - H_bubble) = 150 mol/s * 30.63 kJ/mol = 4594.3 kW (the total condenser removes V of that: 6125.74 kW).
